Subject: Commercial appendix questions — consumption & overage treatment

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the RFP response packet — Procurement has a few clarifying questions on the commercial appendix before we score vendors. Can you confirm the following items and provide concrete language we can drop into the SOW/contract?

1) Consumption unit definition: are tokens counted as input+output? Any deviation for streaming/chat workloads?
2) Commit smoothing / graceband: you list a 20% graceband in the template — is that fixed or negotiable, and how do credits apply if usage spikes then falls?
3) True-up cadence: do you support monthly true-ups vs quarterly true-ups and what pricing applies for overages under each cadence?
4) Overage crediting: any mechanism for partial credits (buffer credits, carry-forward credits) within a 12-month period?
5) Example math: can you provide a worked example for a 100M token/month commit with a 150M spike in month 3 and then 60M in month 4?

Procurement would appreciate contract-ready phrasing and a single-sheet pricing model. I've attached the RFP commercial appendix for reference.

Thanks —
Susan

Subject: Re: Commercial appendix questions — consumption & overage treatment

Hi Susan — great questions. Below is a consolidated commercial proposal and contract-ready phrasing you can drop into the RFP response. I've also attached a one-sheet pricing model (pricing-models-20260916.xlsx) with worked examples.

Summary of our recommended commercial model (proposal):
- Unit: tokens = input + output (counted at final post-tokenization). Streaming/chat: same counting model; streaming increments billed per emitted token.
- Commit tiers: customers commit to a monthly average token volume (e.g., 100M tokens/month) for a 12-month term. Committed unit price is agreed up-front.
- Graceband (smoothing): 20% monthly graceband applied to committed quantity (configurable). Within the 12-month term we also offer a 10% carry-forward pool to absorb shortfalls/overages over 3-month windows.
- True-up cadence: monthly or quarterly true-up supported. Pricing for overages differs: monthly true-up overage = pay-as-you-go rate (no discount). Quarterly true-up overage = blended overage credit: 60% of the committed unit discount is retained as a credit against quarterly overages (i.e., overage billed at 40% of the committed discount penalty, see example).
- Overage handling: we propose two options for legal language — a strict pay-as-you-go overage or a "smoothing + buffer" approach that grants limited credits and carry-forward at the enterprise level.

Worked example (100M commit/month, committed price $0.00040/token, pay-as-you-go price $0.00060/token):
- Month 1 usage 100M -> billed at committed rate: $40,000.
- Month 2 usage 150M (50M over): with monthly true-up -> 50M * $0.00060 = $30,000 overage.
- With quarterly true-up & smoothing: assume quarter total 100+150+60 = 310M vs quarter commit 300M -> net overage 10M. Overage billed at blended overage rate: 10M * ($0.00060 - credit) — credit equals 60% of committed discount (in this example credit ~= $0.00012), resulting in effective overage unit ~= $0.00048 -> $4,800.

Contract wording (draft, pick A or B):
A) Standard monthly true-up (simpler):
"Customer commits to a monthly average consumption of X tokens at the committed unit price. Monthly consumption above the committed quantity shall be billed at the Supplier's standard pay-as-you-go rate."

B) Smoothing + quarterly true-up (preferred for variable workloads):
"Supplier shall apply a monthly graceband of 20% of the committed quantity. Additionally, Supplier will maintain a carry-forward buffer equal to 10% of the annual committed quantity to be applied across any consecutive 3-month window. Consumption above the aggregated commitment for a true-up period shall be billed at an overage rate equal to the pay-as-you-go rate less a smoothing credit equal to 60% of the committed unit discount."

Next steps: happy to iterate on percentages (graceband, carry-forward, credit %) — ping me which option you prefer and we'll produce a redlined SOW EXHIBIT.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales

Hi Susan — appreciate the quick turn. Attached is a finalized 1-page pricing sheet and a contract exhibit draft (mutual-action-plan-ec-20260918.pdf) with auditable definitions and a hard cap clause. Highlights below:  

- Auditable usage: "Usage shall be measured as input tokens + output tokens post-tokenization using Supplier's accounting system; Supplier will provide a monthly usage report and provide raw accounting logs via secure S3 link for any dispute."
- Carry-forward buffer language (excerpt): "A Carry-Forward Buffer equal to 10% of the Customer's annual committed quantity shall be maintained and applied to any consecutive 3-month true-up period. Buffer allocation and remaining balance shall be reported in the monthly reconciliation statement."
- Hard-cap protection: "Supplier guarantees that any invoice amount for a given month, after application of smoothing credits and carry-forward buffer, shall not exceed 150% of the committed monthly charge for that month. This cap applies exclusively to overage charges and does not alter base committed pricing."

Worked example (finalized numbers):
Commit: 100,000,000 tokens/month at $0.00040/token -> committed monthly charge = $40,000.
If month spikes to 150M and there are no carry-forward credits available, maximum invoice after smoothing credits will not exceed $60,000 (150% cap).

Next steps: we can incorporate this as Exhibit B in the SOW and produce a short redline for the Master Services Agreement. I've also created a HubSpot deal and linked the draft documents: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789

If EC is comfortable, I'm happy to schedule a 30-min call next week with Procurement and Legal to run the exhibit.

Cheers,
